--- Codex A (lane the core data model + domain logic — data structures, state management, persistence, and business rules) ---
Implemented on this wave for the data-domain lane.

What works now:

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
Built the real token file — nothing to compile-check here since sandboxed `swiftc` needs separate approval, but I've proofread it against the exact `Theme` contract from interfaces.json.

**What I built this iteration:**
- `DesignSystem/Theme.swift` — the canonical `Theme` enum from interfaces.json, fully populated (not stubbed): `Fonts` (Dynamic-Type-mapped, no fixed points), `Spacing` (4pt grid), `Radius` (card=8, pile=10, button=12, toast=14, panel=18, modal=22 per DEC-design_handoff-002), `Colors.Scene`/`.light`/`.dark` as two genuinely distinct lighting scenes (daylight-through-window vs. lamp-at-night, not an inverted palette, per DEC-design_discussion-002), and `Card` as fixed constants with zero light/dark variation per DEC-design_handoff-001 (glyph ink zone stays flat/high-contrast, no wash).
- `DesignSystem/Layout.swift` — the `cardWidth(contentWidth:)` free function from interfaces.json, clamped to [44,56]pt.
- Deleted the placeholder `DesignSystem.swift` (root) so there's exactly one styling source, per PROJECT_CONVENTIONS.md rule #1 — everything routes through `Theme.*` now, no `DS.*`.

**Flagging something real for Codex A before more Domain code lands on it:** `Domain/DomainTypes.swift` implements `GameState.piles: [PileID: [Card]]` — that's the *original* tech_specs draft shape, but `DEC-project_plan-002` explicitly superseded it with a named-field struct (`stock`, `waste`, `foundations: [Suit:[Card]]`, `tableau: [[Card]]`) specifically because Swift's synthesized `Codable` for a `PileID`-keyed dictionary (enum with associated values) falls back to a flat unkeyed array on encode — non-inspectable JSON, no guaranteed order, and it breaks `RestoreIntegrityService`'s ability to enumerate fixed fields. That decision already shipped with an explicit constraint that `RestoreIntegrityService` and all pile-iterating logic use named fields, not dictionary iteration. Right now `RestoreIntegrityService.swift`, `MoveValidation.swift`, and `StuckDetection.swift` are all written against `state.piles[...]`/`for (pile, cards) in state.piles` — four files built on the shape the pipeline already rejected. Worth fixing now, before Persistence/UI code (mine included — I'll need to iterate `tableau`/`foundations` to render columns and bind `game.tableau.column0.topCard` / `game.foundation.hearts` flow tokens) builds against the wrong pile representation and this has to be reworked twice.

**Left for others/integrator:** I didn't touch `Domain/`, `Persistence/`, or `ci/` (Codex A/B's lanes) — just naming the GameState issue, not fixing it myself. GameView/CardView/StatsView/SettingsView can't be built yet since `GameEngine`, `Card`, `PileID` etc. don't exist as compiled Domain code I can safely link against this wave — next iteration, once the pile-shape question is settled, I'll build `SolitaireTabHost`, `GameView`, and `CardView` against the corrected `GameState`.

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Nice timing — while I was working, Codex A dropped the domain types (`Domain/DomainTypes.swift`, `MoveValidation.swift`, `StuckDetection.swift`, `DeckFactory.swift`, `RestoreIntegrityService.swift`), Claude A landed the real `DesignSystem/Theme.swift` + `Layout.swift`, and Codex B's `Persistence/AtomicFileWriter.swift` was already there. I built T-000 (scaffolding) around that — here's what I did.

**Files created:**
- `ci/dependency_lint.sh` — CI gate that scans every `project.pbxproj` for `XCRemoteSwiftPackageReference` URLs and `Package.resolved` pins, fails on anything not hosted under `github.com/apple/`, `developer.apple.com`, or `swiftlang`, and explicitly bans Alamofire/SwiftyJSON/Realm by name even if someone re-hosts them. Also fails if a stray `Package.swift` shows up at project root. Gracefully no-ops (exit 0) until the `.xcodeproj` exists.
- `Base.lproj/LaunchScreen.storyboard` + `Assets.xcassets/LaunchBackground.colorset/` — a themed launch shell, no white flash. I initially picked my own felt-green guess, then found Claude A's real `Theme.swift` mid-turn and re-synced both the storyboard's inline `namedColor` and the asset catalog to the *exact* numeric values of `Theme.Colors.{light,dark}.surfaceBase` (0.11/0.32/0.22 light, 0.07/0.24/0.15 dark) so there's zero color pop between the storyboard and the real first SwiftUI frame.
- `Info.plist` — zero permission keys, zero background modes, no ATT key (per `[REDACTED:high_entropy]`), portrait-only orientation (`[REDACTED:high_entropy]`), `UILaunchStoryboardName = LaunchScreen`.
- `App/RootPlaceholderView.swift` — a themed placeholder root view (reads `Color("LaunchBackground")`, not a hardcoded literal) for the integrator to point `@main` at until `SolitaireTabHost`/`AppRestoreCoordinator` exist.
- Folder skeleton: `Domain/`, `Features/Game|Stats|Settings/`, `Interaction/`, `DebugTools/`, `Tests/UnitTests|UITests/`, each with a short `README.md` naming the owning lane and what belongs there (mainly so nobody invents a stray top-level folder).
- `MODULES.md` — the canonical ownership table, corrected once Theme.swift landed to describe the real `DesignSystem/` folder instead of the stale flat-file assumption.

**What works now:** the non-project half of "blank card-table-colored screen" is real and design-locked (both storyboard and SwiftUI placeholder pull the identical felt-green token). The dependency lint script is logically complete and will actually gate CI once wired in.

**What remains — explicitly for the integrator, not me:** I did not touch `.xcodeproj`/`project.pbxproj`, `Package.swift`, or `SolitaireAtelierApp.swift` per the lane rules, so none of this is buildable yet. Integrator needs to: create `SolitaireAtelier.xcodeproj` referencing these folders/files as groups, wire `Info.plist` (or port its keys into `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE` build settings), set `UILaunchStoryboardName`, include `Assets.xcassets`, add unit+UI test targets, set `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED/REQUIRED = YES`, `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic`, a real `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`, a reverse-DNS bundle id, point `@main`'s body at `RootPlaceholderView()` for now, and add `ci/dependency_lint.sh` as a Run Script phase. I also couldn't `chmod +x` the lint script or execute it to smoke-test — sandbox blocked script execution this round, so it's only been reviewed by eye, not run; someone should `bash ci/dependency_lint.sh` once the project exists to confirm it behaves.

**How to verify once integrator wires it up:** build the target — it should launch straight to the felt-green screen (not white), zero warnings; run `bash ci/dependency_lint.sh` from repo root — should print `PASS` with no packages present.

2. `MoveValidation.swift`, `RestoreIntegrityService.swift`, and `StuckDetection.swift` are written around `state.piles[...]`/dictionary iteration, so they will fail contract alignment once named-field `GameState` is enforced.

3. `Card` vs `PlayCard` coexist in Domain; this is an interface boundary risk for `GameEngine` + UI move/render layers unless one runtime model is canonicalized and adapters are explicit.

4. Legacy `PileType`-based call paths are still called out as unresolved; without a compatibility adapter layer (`toBoardState`/`toGameState`), integrations between Domain and older lanes will split.

5. Potential duplicate entry-point conflict: `RootPlaceholderView.swift` + `LaunchScreen.storyboard` are ready, but no `@main` wiring exists yet; integrator must ensure exactly one launch root path is used while host views are not yet present.

7. `ci/dependency_lint.sh` appears logically sound but was not executed and may lack execute bit in workspace; integrate it as a run phase only after project creation and run once to confirm it passes real project files.
